policy: Low-confidence pattern matches are PARKED here, never dropped (Law 1: recall beats report-tidiness). Confidence is about whether the pattern APPLIES, not about how bad it is if it does. Adjudicate by hand or at a higher reasoning tier; do not noise-filter this file.

manualReview.description: The pot remains winner-take-all on a purely numeric `count >= nudgeSize` gate, so a searcher who sees a qualifying batchMint in the mempool can front-run it with their own qualifying batch and take the entire multi-token payout. The `minRewards` floor added in the prior cycle (and generalised per-token here) protects the LOSER from paying mint costs for an empty pot, but the contract's own NatSpec states it 'does NOT stop a front-runner from winning the pot'. Ledger L-05 (wont-fix) records that `minReward == 0` is the default opt-out, so a UI or integrator that omits floors reinstates the full exposure.
manualReview.priorArt: Ledger M-01 (medium, FIXED) 'MEV / first-claimer front-run of winner-take-all nudge pot' + L-05 (low, WONT-FIX) 'minReward==0 default silently opts out of the slippage guard'. Memory note phoenix-nft-staking-batchminter-nudge records that the MEV front-run survives by design.
manualReview.whyParked: Same root cause as an already-triaged ledger entry, re-expressed across N tokens rather than 1. Needs a human decision on whether the multi-token generalisation changes the M-01 disposition or is a pure echo.
manualReview.adjudicationQuestion: Does per-token `minRewards` over N tokens change the M-01 fixed disposition, or is this the documented residual?

manualReview.status: REFUTED-WITH-SOURCE (parked so it is not re-derived from scratch next run)
manualReview.description: Between step 6 (`forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max)`) and step 8 (`forceApprove(nftMinter, 0)`) the contract holds a live unlimited payment-token approval, and the mint loop inside that window fires `onERC1155Received` on a fully caller-controlled `recipient`. The question is whether that callback can cause the minter to spend BatchNFTMinter's allowance. REFUTATION: `NFTMinterV2.mint` pulls with `IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, config.dispatcher, price)` - the payer is always `msg.sender`, so a reentrant call from the recipient hook pays from the hook's own balance, not from BatchNFTMinter's allowance. The only other mint path, `mintFor`, is `authorizedMinters`-gated and moves no funds. Reentry back into `batchMint` itself is now blocked by the story-022 `nonReentrant`.
manualReview.whyParked: Refuted against sibling-repo source rather than by a PoC, and the refutation depends on NFTMinterV2 keeping `msg.sender` as the payer. If NFTMinterV2 ever gains an arbitrary-`from` pull, this becomes live. Parked as a standing watch, not as a finding.
manualReview.watchTrigger: Any NFTMinterV2 change introducing a `from`/`payer` parameter, or a new authorizedMinter path that spends third-party allowances.

manualReview.description: `_payRewards` makes an external call to a fully caller-supplied address (`IERC20(rewardTokens[i]).safeTransfer`), and `_snapshotRewards` calls `balanceOf` on the same. This is an arbitrary-code hook the caller controls, executing after the payment-token approval is revoked (step 8) but before the dust sweep (step 10). `nonReentrant` blocks reentry into `batchMint`; every other state-changing function is onlyOwner or onlyPauser; the snapshot pass is `view` so it cannot reenter at all. No exploitable sibling was identified. Residual surface worth a second pass: the callback fires while this contract still holds the un-swept payment-token residue, and while any in-flight dispatcher/hook state from the just-completed mint loop is settled but externally observable.
manualReview.whyParked: No concrete exploit path found, but the pattern's `vulnerableWhen` ('function A makes an external call ... sibling function B reads that state') is partially satisfied and the sibling set should be re-checked whenever a new non-owner entrypoint is added to this contract.
manualReview.watchTrigger: Any new external/public non-owner function added to BatchNFTMinter.

manualReview.description: Two coupled niggles in step 10. (a) The sweep is `paymentToken.balanceOf(address(this))`, not the caller's unspent budget, so a third-party donation or accumulated sub-threshold dust is swept to `msg.sender` alongside their own refund, with no `nudgeSize` gate. Documented as intended ('a griefer who pre-deposits payment-token simply donates to the next caller'). (b) Consequently the `totalPaid` return value - `paymentAmount > remaining ? paymentAmount - remaining : 0` - understates (and can floor to 0) the caller's actual net spend whenever `remaining` includes value that was not theirs, which is wrong for any integrator or accounting UI consuming it.
manualReview.whyParked: The narrow reading is documented-as-intended and QA-grade; it is filed here rather than dropped because it is the same mechanism that PATTERN-002 escalates to potential-high under a different dispatcher configuration. Adjudicate the two together.

manualReview.description: On a non-qualifying batch (`qualifies == false`) `available` is pinned to `0`, so ANY non-zero `minRewards[i]` reverts `BatchMint__RewardBelowMinimum` even though the caller asked for no nudge and simply wants to mint. Likewise the payment-token exclusion fires unconditionally, including when `nudgeSize == 0` disables the feature outright. Both are now DOCUMENTED as deliberate (the unconditional exclusion is a balance-probing defence per §4.1). Recorded as the descendant of the previously-submitted L-03.
manualReview.priorArt: Ledger L-03 (low, submitted) 'Nudge-token equality guard reverts even when nudge is size-disabled'. Story-022 kept the behaviour and added a rationale, so this may now be a documented-intent closure rather than a live finding.
manualReview.whyParked: Needs a human call on whether the added rationale closes the submitted L-03 or merely restates it.

manualReview.description: `emergencyWithdraw` decrements `totalStaked` but calls neither `_updatePool` nor `_recomputeSchedule`, so `rewardRate` stays sized against the pre-exit `totalStaked` until the next interaction, over-emitting to the survivors in the interim. This is the M-02 root cause recurring on the FOURTH hand-maintained copy of NFTStaker.
manualReview.DISCLOSURE-REQUIRED: This root cause was triaged WONT-FIX by the owner on a prior contract. Ledger M-02 (medium, wont-fix) 'emergencyWithdraw skips _recomputeSchedule/_updatePool, leaving stale rewardRate' - owner-acknowledged 2026-06-09 on the grounds that the contract is already deployed, there is no migrate-on-behalf, and pullAndRefresh mitigates. A second ledger entry, '[SUPPRESSED-CONTEXT] Inherited emergencyWithdraw over-emission on NFTStakerPriceScaled', was closed as false-positive on the same grounds. A NEW contract mints a NEW fingerprint that dedup will NOT link, so if this is re-filed the prior triage MUST be named and its reason quoted, per the standing 'disclose when re-filing an owner wont-fix' rule. Do not silently override the reclassNote.
manualReview.reFileBasis: The two owner grounds do not transfer cleanly: NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady is NOT yet deployed (it is new this cycle, so the 'already deployed' argument does not apply), and it DOES have migrate-on-behalf (`batchMigrate` / `depositFor`), which was the second stated ground. That is a genuine basis for re-evaluation rather than an echo - hence parked for human adjudication rather than auto-suppressed.
manualReview.whyParked: Confidence is low that this should be re-opened as a finding, but the disposition change is material enough that silently suppressing it would violate Law 1.

manualReview.description: `rescueERC20`, when the rescued token IS the reward token, calls `_updatePool()` then `_recomputeSchedule()` DIRECTLY - not `_recomputeScheduleIfActive()`. Called while `Migrating`, it therefore moves `rewardRate` / `windowEnd` / `rewardBudget` off the `initiateMigration` snapshot that the contract's own NatSpec says must stay pinned ('the frozen snapshot's rewardRate / windowEnd / rewardBudget cannot move while Migrating'). The NatSpec on `_recomputeScheduleIfActive` calls the owner-driven recomputes 'deliberate', so this may be intended. No accrual harm is apparent because `_updatePool` no-ops while `Migrating` and `finalizeAndReset` recomputes again on the way out; the exposure is a divergence between the documented invariant and the code, plus the `committedDebt` solvency check being evaluated against a mid-freeze budget.
manualReview.whyParked: Reads as an intended owner path with an unclear invariant boundary. Needs a story-faithfulness call on whether 'frozen while Migrating' is meant to admit owner exceptions.

manualReview.description: `initiateMigration` calls `_syncBudget()`, which invokes `dispatcherHook.pull()` with no try/catch. A reverting, unauthorised, or paused hook therefore blocks the migration from being engaged at all - the one moment an operator most needs it to work. Same shape for `depositFor`, which also runs `_syncBudget()` at its head. `emergencyWithdraw` remains available as the escape hatch, so principal is not trapped.
manualReview.priorArt: Recurrence of ledger L-02 (open, Low) 'NFTStakerDepletion._syncBudget un-try/catch'd dispatcherHook.pull() lets an unau...' filed against the depletion copy in run-18. New contract, new fingerprint.
manualReview.whyParked: Confidence low that this rises above the existing Low on the sibling copy; parked so the recurrence on a fourth copy is visible rather than deduped away.

manualReview.description: This cycle adds a FOURTH hand-maintained copy of NFTStaker (NFTStaker -> NFTStakerPriceScaled -> NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady, plus NFTStakerDepletion). The new file is a copy of a copy: it is NFTStakerPriceScaled verbatim plus the story-019 migration block, and NFTStakerPriceScaled is itself a hand-maintained copy of NFTStaker. The contract's own header states 'Any future fix or audit change to either is NOT automatically inherited'. Diffing this run confirmed the deltas are confined to the eight documented items (name/interface, migration block, _safePayTo, freeze hooks, rescueERC20, and the three price-scaled specific recompute routings) with no unintended drift.
